title: Sefer ha-Zohar (Hebrew, Lublin 1882 print)
author: Moses de Leon
description: Sefer ha-Zohar (The Book of Radiance), here in a Hebrew-Aramaic printed edition from Lublin, 1882. The Zohar is the central work of Kabbalah, a vast mystical commentary on the Torah written in Aramaic in late thirteenth-century Castile, attributed by tradition to the second-century sage Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai and his companions, but identified by modern scholarship with Moses de León and his circle. Organised by the weekly Torah portions, it combines biblical interpretation, narratives of the wandering companions, and treatises on the sefirot and the inner life of God, the divine names, the Ein Sof, the masculine and feminine aspects of the divine and their union, the Shekhinah in exile, the origin of evil (the Other Side), the soul and its destiny, and the mystical meaning of the commandments. The Lublin edition follows the standard pagination of the classic Mantua and Cremona printings.
